name: Nick Hess

bio.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement lists occupation as community revitalization consultant, with an occupational background in renewable energy operations management.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Community Revitalization Consultant Occupational Background: Renewable Energy Operations Management

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

bio.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement lists prior governmental experience on the Milwaukie Planning Commission and as Treasurer of the Downtown Alliance of Milwaukie.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Milwaukie Planning Commission; Treasurer, Downtown Alliance of Milwaukie

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

bio.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement says Hess was born and raised in Milwaukie and is raising three children there while the children attend public schools.
bio.excerpt: I was born and raised in Milwaukie and my wife and I are proud to raise our three children here while they attend our public schools.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

positions.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement says Milwaukie needs a long-term financial plan that protects essential services and spends taxpayer dollars wisely.
positions.excerpt: We need a long-term financial plan that protects essential services, spends taxpayer dollars wisely, and strengthens our local economy.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

positions.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement says the city must maintain streets, sidewalks and infrastructure while improving connections between neighborhoods, parks and businesses.
positions.excerpt: we must maintain the streets, sidewalks, and infrastructure that keep our city functioning while improving connections between neighborhoods, parks, and businesses.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

positions.statement: Hess's pamphlet statement says Hess will support local businesses and redevelopment downtown and in neighborhood hubs.
positions.excerpt: I will support local businesses and redevelopment that bring new life to downtown and neighborhood hubs.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 36 (printed C-35)

positions.statement: On the priorities page of Hess's campaign website, Hess describes an approach to housing that combines public, private and nonprofit sectors.
positions.excerpt: Milwaukie should take an all of the above approach that brings together public, private, and nonprofit sectors

verification.note: Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns). Page undated.

positions.statement: On the priorities page of Hess's campaign website, Hess says residents should see progress on Milwaukie Bay Park while the parks district is held accountable.
positions.excerpt: Milwaukie residents deserve to see real progress on Milwaukie Bay Park while ensuring NCPRD is accountable

verification.note: Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns). Page undated. NCPRD expanded in the statement as 'parks district'.

gaps: No position found on public safety or transportation beyond pamphlet infrastructure line
Pamphlet also lists 'over 15 Milwaukie Business Owners' as supporters (unnamed group, not recorded)
